title: soft-threshold-slab-partitioner: length-aware slab partitioning to reduce padding waste
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a soft-threshold slab partitioner for sequence-length-driven batching that reduces padding tokens and improves p95 latency on mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible config flag (disabled by default).
description: Summary: This PR adds a soft-threshold slab partitioner to the runtime batcher that groups incoming requests into variable-width slabs by sequence length distribution. The goal is to reduce padding overhead while avoiding brittle hard bucket boundaries and to surface lightweight kernel-selection hints for packed lane execution. Motivation: Existing fixed bucketing either over-fragments or forces heavy padding at the tail of mixed-length workloads. We observed customer workloads with bimodal distributions (short chat queries + long document summarizations) where worst-case padding accounted for 12-18% of token cost. Design: The slab partitioner forms contiguous length ranges (slabs) with an adaptive soft threshold: each slab has a target max-pad ratio (configurable, default 0.12). Incoming requests are first routed to an active slab based on length; slabs accept small overflows for a short time window (soft threshold) before creating a new slab, which reduces churn for lengths near boundaries. Key behaviors: 1) soft thresholds avoid frequent slab creation on noisy length borders; 2) each slab tracks average length and pad ratio and emits kernel-selection hints for packed kernels (e.g., prefer lane-packed conv kernels when >60% lanes above the slab median); 3) a lightweight prefill probe queries KV-cache prefetch priority for high-length slabs to avoid pop-and-wait on first-token cold paths. Configuration: runtime/batcher/slab_partitioner: enabled=false (default), max_pad_ratio=0.12, soft_threshold_ms=30, min_slab_size=8. API: no surface changes to public inference API; config exposed via console and runtime flags. Benchmarks: MixedChatDocs workload (60% short seq <=64, 35% mid 128-512, 5% long >1024) on p4d.24xlarge: - Token-cost (estimated per-100k tokens): -9.1% vs mainline fixed-quantile bucketing - P95 latency at 1000 QPS: -7.4% (from 223ms -> 206ms) - Median latency: -5.8% - Throughput (sustained tokens/sec): +6.3% Notes: improvements concentrated where mid/long tail intermix; pure-short workloads see neutral change. Backwards compatibility: feature off by default; KV-keying unchanged.
